text.p: The central bank lent banks a total of 35.1 trillion lira via overnight and tomorrow/next deals to meet rising demand from state banks caused by 64 trillion lira of public sector salaries paid on Wednesday.
The bank funded 18.3 trillion lira via overnight at 77 percent and 16.8 trillion lira via t/n deals at 72 percent on the interbank for the first time this year.
The central bank, which had mostly drained excess cash in the last two weeks because of high liquidity, had withdrawn 6.6 trillion lira at 56 percent on Tuesday.
Bankers said strong cash demand by state banks to meet public sector salary payments squeezed the market sharply despite a 23.2 trillion lira surplus at the opening.
The average overnight money rate jumped to 74.44 percent from yesterday's 57.95.
Bankers said the central bank's minor dollar sales to a few banks at above 112,400 lira in the afternon also drained some money from the market.
The lira closed at 112,400 to the dollar, easing from 112,200 at the opening and 111,750 at Tuesday's close in line with the dollar's surge to 1.6000 marks in world markets.

Bond yields edged higher for a third consecutive day, but bankers said trade remained quiet and was overwhelmingly dominated by February 11, 1998 paper, whose average yield firmed to 96.34 percent from Tuesday's 95.87 percent.
The second most heavily traded October 30, 1997 paper yielded 94.18 percent, up from Tuesday's 93.87 average.
